$comment: Single source of truth. `npm run tokens` generates src/panel/tokens.css from this. Never hand-edit the CSS. Contrast ratios are measured against --canvas unless noted.

ground.means: V2.4 VB-111 — the ONE app-wide canvas every surface sits on; white (--canvas) survives only inside buttons, inputs and cards

ink-3.means: V2.4 VB-111: darkened from #6B7484 (4.7:1 on white) so it clears 4.5:1 with margin on --ground, the app-wide canvas

divider.role: decorative separators only — NOT for control boundaries

dock-edge.role: V1.4 VB-22. The interactive boundary INSIDE the file drawer's chrome, where the ground is the drawer's own stage rather than the canvas. --border-i's 3.13:1 is measured against --canvas and falls to 2.92:1 on --surface, which is the stage List's bar and nav take — under the 3:1 floor, so the dock steps once further down the same neutral ramp. Nowhere else: on the canvas --border-i is still the boundary.

select-ring.role: V2.5 VB-118/VB-122. The selector suite's interactive boundary — the tile grammar's radio ring and the divided line's option edge — which sits on the app-wide --ground (3.51:1) and on --sunken hover/left-side washes (3.27:1). Same physics as dock-edge, measured on this stage: --border-i clears 3:1 only on --canvas and falls to 2.92:1 on --ground, so the suite steps down the same neutral ramp. Same value as dock-edge on purpose — one ramp, two named stages — but its own token, because dock-edge's role note fences it to the drawer and a shared literal would weld the two roles together.

primary.means: Workbrain is asking you to act

violet.means: this belongs to your AI — read only

amber.means: time is asking you to act — drift, staleness

green-strong.means: V1.1 VB-07. The same 'done, current, healthy' family at full strength — the file tree's ACTIVE section against --green's already-reached ones. Reached vs current has to read as one colour at two strengths, not 'coloured vs grey' (the ported design). On a light canvas 'stronger' is deeper, not lighter: the sibling app mixes its accent toward white for the weaker state because it sits on a dark surface, and doing that here would push the weaker state under 4.5:1.

danger.means: something failed and you can fix it. Field errors only.

overlay.role: Sheet backdrop only — the one overlay in the system

toast-check.role: checkmark color inside a Toast, which sits on --ink

brand.$comment: V1.1 VB-01. The Model Citizen node-graph mark, redrawn from ../modelcitizen/public/mark.svg. This is the one multi-colour thing in the system and the only reason a nested colour group exists — every other colour above carries a single meaning the interface uses to say something. These say nothing: the mark is decorative (aria-hidden) and always sits next to the real 'Workbrain' wordmark, so no contrast ratio is claimed and none is needed. Never use one of these for text, an interactive boundary, or a state. Five gradient pairs + one edge stroke, matching the source export exactly.

edge.role: the graph's connecting lines — carried at a per-line stroke-opacity that fakes depth

service.$comment: V2.4 VB-105. The service-chip persona palette — the third nested colour group, and scoped for the same reason as `brand`: these are costumes, not meanings. Each AI service's chip wears one persona — ChatGPT Aristocrat, Claude Scholar, Gemini Muse, Copilot Colleague, Grok Investigator, Perplexity Explorer, Other Innovator (docs/V2.4-REFINEMENT.md, decision 2; the key->persona map is core/flow/serviceThemes.ts). DESIGN-ONLY by decision (FLAG 4): the persona never prints, never speaks, and never carries a meaning the chip's label doesn't — so no persona colour may ever be used to SAY something elsewhere in the interface. Two values per persona: the tone (icon stroke at rest, chip fill when selected, hover border) and its tint (hover/selected wash). Every tone is measured >= 4.5:1 against --canvas, which is the same floor twice over: as the selected chip's ground under --ink-inv text, and as a hover border it clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 with room. Tints are washes under --ink text (all >= 15:1, measured) and claim no contrast of their own.

home.$comment: V2.6 VB-125. The two file-identity accents on Home's cards — Context and Skills — scoped for the persona-palette's reason (V2.4 FLAG 4 precedent): costumes, not meanings. Each dresses ONE card's chip, hairline bar and go-verb; the card's STATE is said in words with the semantic colours (green=current, amber=partly), so nothing is ever said by these. Adopted from Adam's template (docs/workbrain-panel.html) with two near-misses accepted deliberately and fenced here: `context` sits near --green and `skills` near --primary — on Home's cards only, never state-bearing, never elsewhere. Actions' accent is NOT here because the system already owns the right colour: --violet ('belongs to your AI — read only') is literally what the derived Actions.md is. Tones measured as text on --canvas (the shell) and on their own tint; tints are washes under the tone's icon strokes.

context.means: Context.md's costume. 4.73:1 on its own tint.

skills.means: Skills.md's costume. 5.25:1 on its own tint.

splash.$comment: V2.7 VB-128/129. The splash show's own dark stage — the second sanctioned dark surface after the drawer's, fenced to the splash exactly as `globe` is fenced to the drawer. `field` is the world the shard show flies in and the reveal settles onto; the reveal's ink is --ink-inv (white, ~18:1 here) and the quiet lines ride white at alphas that all clear 4.5:1 on this near-black. `focus` is the ring on that field — the globe stage's own focus value, re-tokened per the select-ring precedent. The `scene-*` entries are the shard windows' procedural paintings (VB-129): SCENERY, not meanings — a portrait's skin and wood, office cool light, paper, a bank header's navy, a document's soft ink — read at runtime by SplashStage's painters the way WallPanels reads its texture hues, and claiming no contrast because nothing rests on them (the paintings are aria-hidden glass behind VB-130's photography, and its silent fallback). Never use one to SAY anything.

focus.role: focus ring on the splash field

link.role: the path into the reveal's second section, the words it hands to, and the line under the answer
link.means: V2.9 slice 3d (Adam, 2026-09-01: "fuscia or dark hot pink"). ONE COLOUR SAYING ONE THING — a through-line down the screen. It is the connector that draws from the minutes into the claim, it is where the gradient on START TO FINISH begins, and it is the line under NOTHING at the end. The eye is meant to follow it: the first connector is cyan and belongs to the section above, this one is not, and the change of colour is what marks the hand-off. It replaces --splash-start (a green on the word "start") and --splash-answer (an orange underline), which said two unrelated things in two hues where this says one thing three times. Measured 6.50:1 on --splash-field; the gradient it opens never drops below 6.01:1 across its length.

peak-blue.means: W Peaks' middle peak (the shipped icon, 2026-09-02) - the one member of the icon's triad without an existing token (aqua is --globe-node-2-solid, purple is --splash-link-end). Scenery-only: the voice mark and the intro's animated peaks paint with it; nothing textual rests on it.

homage-chatgpt.means: V3.0 pass 3k - the six 'homage' hues: each service's theme-color VIBE (Adam: 'the color of the visual changes to that apps theme color vibe, like an homage'), painting the drawn mocks and chip washes on the baseline errand. Scenery only, aria-hidden or decorative in every use - state never rides them, so no contrast floor applies. Approximations by design: a nod, not a brand claim.

homage-chatgpt-ink.means: V3.0 pass 3l - the homage hues' TEXT-GRADE siblings: the same vibes darkened until they clear 4.5:1 on --canvas, because the service picker now sets the NAMES in their colors (wordmark-style links, the modern SaaS integration-picker pattern) and words are held to the text floor where washes were not. grok reuses its scenery hue - already ink-dark.

you-ink.means: The intro card's member of the link-end purple family. The card sits on the WHITE canvas, where #B36BFF measures 3.24:1 - fine as an underline, failing as text - so the 'you do' mark darkens to hold the hue and clear the floor. Measured 4.92:1 on --canvas.

ai-ink.means: The intro card's member of the aqua family (--globe-node-2-solid is 1.75:1 on white, purely a dark-stage colour). 'your AI does' on the white canvas wears this instead. Measured 5.02:1 on --canvas.

link-end.role: where the gradient on START TO FINISH arrives
link-end.means: V2.9 slice 3d. The far end of --splash-link: the words travel from the colour of the path that led to them into a purple, so the sentence itself is the last leg of the journey down the page. Measured 6.09:1 on --splash-field. Nothing is distinguished by this colour alone — the words are the words, and the gradient is emphasis on a line that is fully legible without it.

globe.$comment: V1.2 VB-14. The Brain globe's own palette — the second and last nested colour group, for the same reason as `brand` above: these are the parts of one picture, not meanings the interface uses to say something. Deliberately NOT the `brand` values. Those were sampled from a flat single-pose export on a white page and are light enough to disappear against each other once a node is a shaded sphere; docs/V1.2-REFINEMENT.md's VB-14 iteration three picks a deeper palette and a dark stage on purpose, and calls that stage 'the one sanctioned dark surface in the product, contained inside the drawer'. Each sphere is a three-stop radial: `highlight` (shared, offset off-centre), then its own `mid`, then its own `deep` at the rim — a pair per sphere plus one highlight, which is what makes a node read as lit rather than as a flat disc. `label` and `focus` are the only two here that carry information, and both are measured against `field`. V1.4 VB-22 widened this group's job from 'the globe's palette' to 'the dark stage's palette': the drawer's whole chrome — its mode bar, its section count, its grip, and the docked nav's buttons above it — is one surface with the stage, so it dresses in `field`, `panel`, `label`, `detail-key` and `focus` rather than in a second dark palette that would have to agree with this one. V1.5 VB-24 turned the five `*-solid` values up — an answered orb had to read as lit rather than as coloured — and added a `*-muted` beside each one, because an unanswered node stopped being a hollow ring and became the same orb turned down: same hue, ~44% of the way to the stage's own slate, which measures a hair under half an answered orb's luminance at every depth while staying an object against the field. VB-25 added `unified*` for the one colour the whole model resolves to when the file is complete and current.

glow-live.$comment: R-07. The halo a STARTED section wears, and the colour its four-second breath moves through. Blue rather than the ring's green on purpose: green is this palette's DONE (see `glow-done` and `--globe-ring`), and a started section that glowed green would be claiming to be finished. Chosen against `field` at the two opacities the pulse runs between, so the quiet end is still visible and the loud end is still a glow rather than a flare.

glow-done.$comment: R-07. The halo a COMPLETE section wears. The unified glow's own family (`unified*` below), because a complete section is one of the parts that eventually becomes that single lit object — the stage should not introduce a fourth green to say a third time what `--globe-ring` and `unified` already say.

unified.role: V1.5 VB-25. The one colour the whole model resolves to when every section is answered, complete and fresh — every orb, every edge and every bloom at once, so the solid reads as one lit object instead of a network of differently-lit parts. Brighter and whiter than any of the five node colours on purpose: the change has to be obvious without being a flourish. It is a STATE and never a reward (docs/GUARDRAILS.md) — losing it says 'something is out of date', never anything about the person.

unified-mid.role: the bloom behind a unified orb — `unified`'s own mid, so the light around an orb is the light in it

unified-deep.role: what the back of a unified orb sinks toward. The same depth cue every orb already has (`brainglobe-shade`), in the unified colour's own deep — one colour must not mean one flat drawing.

highlight.role: the specular dot every sphere shares, offset to 34%/30% so all twelve are lit from one place

field.role: the deep-field stage the globe sits on — and, since V1.9 VB-50, the whole drawer around it. V2.0 VB-69 removed `field-glow`, the lighter centre of a radial that used to paint the stage's own box: a soft gradient inside a hard rectangle is still a rectangle, and this is the one field the picture and the drawer share.

edge.role: a near edge of the solid

edge-far.role: a far edge — depth is carried by colour as well as width and opacity

label.role: section labels on `field`. Depth dims them to 0.72 opacity at the very back, which still measures 8.81:1 — far must read as far without dropping below 4.5:1.

focus.role: the focus ring inside the stage. --primary is the panel's ring everywhere else and measures 2.90:1 on this field — under the 3:1 floor for a non-text indicator — so the dark stage gets an equal-or-better replacement rather than a ring nobody can find (docs/GUARDRAILS.md).

ring.role: the halo on the section being written now. Never the only signal — the halo is a shape, and the state is in the node's accessible name too.

panel.role: V1.4 VB-23. The surface the sub-section detail panel sits on when the stage splits. 1.23:1 on `field` — deliberately near-invisible on its own, because it is a *place* rather than a card, and the hairline below is what actually draws its edge. Non-interactive, so no 3:1 boundary is claimed for it.

panel-line.role: the detail panel's hairline. 1.85:1 on `panel` — a decorative separator, the same job `divider` does on the light canvas, and never a control boundary.

detail-key.role: the question a detail cell answers, on `panel` (9.74:1 on `field` where the panel is see-through). Quieter than `label`'s 13.68:1 so the person's own words are the loud thing in the cell — quieter, never under 4.5:1.

tone-red-tint.means: V2.9 (Adam, 2026-09-02) — the Home row tones. One family per row so the list stops reading as six of the same card. TINT is the chip ground and the hover ground: a wash at the weight the neutral card already had, because the brief was "still just as subtle as current". INK is the icon and label, chosen at a depth that clears 4.5:1 on its own tint AND on the panel ground, so a row is legible at rest and on hover without a second colour. Download keeps the standard treatment and has no entry here.

pop-1.means: V2.9 — THE SPLASH POP PALETTE, softened 2026-09-02. Adam: "the current colors are a little too vibrant and distract too much from the logo during the sequence, I want to draw the eye to it materializing out of the white." The first set was fully saturated and had nowhere to go: a show that opens at full strength cannot build, and cannot hand over to anything quieter. These are the same eight hues at roughly half the saturation and a good deal lighter, so the wall reads as colour without competing with the mark that follows it. Fenced to the splash canvas. — coral

pop-paper.means: The card/sheet inside a drawn panel.

pop-ink.means: Bars, rules and glyph blocks inside a drawn panel. Lightened with the palette so nothing on the wall is near-black.

pop-shade.means: The darker ground a drawn panel can sit on. Lightened with the rest of the palette 2026-09-02 — at near-black it punched a hole through a wall that is meant to be building toward white.

tim-skin.means: V2.9 (Adam, 2026-09-02) — TIM. The narrator gets a face: the control for read-aloud and Jump to, and a ring that pulses on the words as he speaks. Drawn rather than sourced, like the splash panels, so it scales, weighs nothing and needs no licence. Warm mid-brown skin and a soft coiled crown read at 34px without exaggerating any feature — the brief is friendly and plausible with a British accent, and a caricature would fail both.

tim-skin-shade.means: Neck and the shaded side of the face.

tim-hair.means: A soft coiled crown, drawn as a scalloped silhouette rather than as strands.

tim-wear.means: The sweater. Warm, and the one thing in the avatar that is not skin or hair.

tim-line.means: Brows, eyes and the smile. One ink, used sparingly.

pop-tone.means: The single light shade the whole wall opens in, before any colour cuts. A patchwork read before it is a picture read.

sans.value: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Inter, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

mono.value: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

wordmark.use: the 'Workbrain' wordmark on the welcome screen, and nothing else. Deliberately smaller than type.display, which is site-only — 32px is too loud at 400px wide.

question.use: the one question on a panel screen

body.use: instructional text — the floor for anything that tells somebody what to do. Beta review §1.

support.use: body, descriptions, status. Was 13px until the beta review's §1 calibration raised the floor.

fine.use: the smallest text anywhere in the panel. Nothing goes below this.

label.use: section labels, sentence case. Was 12px uppercase with 0.08em tracking until the beta review's §1; the globe's own node labels are exempt and keep the caps, because core/flow/globeLabels.ts computes its truncation budget from that width.

1.use: hover lift on an interactive row

motion.$comment: One easing curve for everything. Three durations. No others.
